title: Comparative world religions
examples: How are Hinduism and Buddhism different?
What do Judaism, Christianity and Islam have in common?
What do different religions believe about life after death?

items: Religion | Ultimate reality | Key text | Goal
Judaism | One God | Torah, Tanakh | Live by God's covenant
Christianity | One God, Trinity | Bible | Salvation through Jesus
Islam | One God, Allah | Qur'an | Submission to God, paradise
Hinduism | Brahman, many forms | Vedas, Gita | Moksha, liberation
Buddhism | No creator God needed | Tripitaka, sutras | Nirvana, end of suffering
Sikhism | One God, Ik Onkar | Guru Granth Sahib | Union with God

explain.say: Comparing religions means describing what each believes and does, fairly and without ranking them. A helpful start is to group them into families: the Abrahamic religions, the Dharmic religions of India, and the traditions of East Asia.

items: Plus Indigenous traditions and non-religious worldviews

explain.say: The Abrahamic religions share a family tree that goes back to Abraham. They believe in one God who created the world, who spoke through prophets, and who will judge people. They differ on who Jesus and Muhammad were.

draw.text: Jews: Jesus was not the Messiah. Christians: Jesus is the Son of God. Muslims: Jesus is a great prophet, and Muhammad the final prophet.

explain.say: The Dharmic religions share ideas like karma, actions having consequences, and samsara, a cycle of birth, death and rebirth. Their goal is release from the cycle, called moksha or nirvana, though they describe it differently.

draw.text: Sikhs also speak of karma and rebirth, and seek union with the one God.

explain.say: Here is a side by side look at beliefs about what happens after death. Abrahamic faiths usually teach one life followed by judgement, while Dharmic faiths usually teach many lives until liberation.

a: Heaven or paradise; hell or separation
Judaism focuses more on this life

explain.say: Practices compare in interesting ways too: prayer, sacred texts, special days, food rules and pilgrimage. And almost every tradition teaches some form of the golden rule: treat others as you would want to be treated.

When comparing, remember three things. Every religion has many branches and individuals who differ. Describe beliefs in the words followers use. And similarities are real, but so are differences that matter deeply to believers.

faq.q: How are Hinduism and Buddhism different?
faq.a: Both come from India and share ideas like karma, rebirth and liberation. But many Hindus worship God or gods, often as forms of one ultimate reality, Brahman, and believe in an eternal self, the atman. Buddhism does not depend on a creator God and teaches anatta, that there is no permanent self, with the goal of nirvana.

faq.q: What do Judaism, Christianity and Islam have in common?
faq.a: All three are Abrahamic religions: they trace their story to Abraham, believe in one God who created the world, honour prophets such as Abraham and Moses, have sacred scriptures, and teach that God will judge humanity. Jerusalem is holy to all three.
asks: what do Jews Christians and Muslims share

faq.q: How are Judaism, Christianity and Islam different?
faq.a: They differ mainly on who Jesus and Muhammad were. Jews await the Messiah and do not see Jesus as the Messiah; Christians believe Jesus is the Messiah and Son of God, part of the Trinity; Muslims honour Jesus as a great prophet and believe Muhammad was the final prophet, who received the Qur'an.

faq.q: What do different religions believe about life after death?
faq.a: Judaism, Christianity and Islam generally teach one earthly life followed by God's judgement, leading to heaven or paradise, or to separation from God; Judaism tends to focus more on this life. Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism and Sikhism teach rebirth shaped by karma, until release from the cycle.
asks: what happens when you die in different religions

faq.q: Do all religions believe in God?
faq.a: No. Judaism, Christianity, Islam and Sikhism believe in one God; many Hindus worship many deities, often as forms of one divine reality; Buddhism and Jainism do not depend on a creator God; and humanists and other non-religious people do not believe in God at all.

faq.q: What is the difference between monotheism and polytheism?
faq.a: Monotheism is belief in one God, as in Judaism, Christianity, Islam and Sikhism. Polytheism is belief in many gods, as in ancient Greek and Norse religion. Hinduism is complex: many Hindus worship many deities, while also understanding them as forms of one supreme reality.

The golden rule is the teaching to treat others as you would want to be treated. Versions appear in Judaism, Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism, Confucianism and humanism, making it one of the most widely shared moral ideas in the world.
asks: treat others as you want to be treated

faq.q: What are the sacred texts of the main religions?
faq.a: Judaism has the Torah and the wider Tanakh; Christianity the Bible, Old and New Testaments; Islam the Qur'an; Hinduism the Vedas, Upanishads and Bhagavad Gita among many; Buddhism the Tripitaka and many sutras; and Sikhism the Guru Granth Sahib.
asks: what is each religion's holy book

faq.q: What do Dharmic religions have in common?
faq.a: Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism and Sikhism all began in India and share ideas like karma, samsara or rebirth, and dharma, the right way of living. Each seeks liberation in its own way, and all value non-violence, though Jainism emphasises it most strongly.

faq.q: How is Sikhism different from Hinduism and Islam?
faq.a: Sikhism is a distinct religion founded by Guru Nanak in the 1400s, not a mix of the two. Sikhs believe in one God, follow the teachings of ten Gurus and the Guru Granth Sahib, and stress equality, honest work, sharing and remembering God. Like Hindus they speak of karma and rebirth, and like Muslims they worship one God.
asks: is Sikhism a mix of Hinduism and Islam

faq.a: Humanism is a non-religious worldview. Humanists do not believe in God or an afterlife, and base their ethics on reason, evidence, empathy and human wellbeing. Many people who are religiously unaffiliated share some humanist ideas.

faq.q: Are all religions basically the same?
faq.a: They share a lot, such as care for others, prayer or meditation, and the search for meaning. But they also differ on important questions, such as whether there is a God, who Jesus was, and what happens after death. Respectful comparison takes both the similarities and the differences seriously.
asks: do all religions teach the same thing

faq.q: How do Jainism and Buddhism compare?
faq.a: Both arose in India around 2,500 years ago, reject the need for a creator God, and aim to end the cycle of rebirth. Jainism teaches an eternal soul, the jiva, and very strict non-violence; Buddhism teaches no permanent self and a middle way between extremes.

Comparative religion is the study of different religions side by side, looking at their beliefs, practices, texts and history, without judging which is true. It helps people understand their neighbours and see both what faiths share and what makes each unique.

facts: Judaism, Christianity and Islam are called Abrahamic religions because they trace their story to Abraham.
Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism and Sikhism began in India and share ideas such as karma and rebirth.
Buddhism teaches anatta, no permanent self; Hinduism teaches an eternal self, the atman.
Muslims honour Jesus as a prophet; Christians believe he is the Son of God.
Versions of the golden rule appear in most of the world's religions and in humanism.

quiz.say: Recall. Which group of religions shares ideas of karma and rebirth?
quiz.show: Which family shares karma and rebirth?
quiz.why: Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism and Sikhism, the Dharmic religions, share ideas of karma and rebirth.

wrong.0: The Abrahamic religions generally teach one life followed by judgement.
wrong.2: Old Norse religion had its own afterlife beliefs, not a karma and rebirth cycle.

quiz.say: Apply. A friend says, I believe in one God who spoke through prophets, and Muhammad was the final prophet. Which religion does this describe?
quiz.show: One God, Muhammad the final prophet: which religion?
quiz.why: Muslims believe in one God, Allah, and that Muhammad was the final prophet, who received the Qur'an.

wrong.0: Judaism believes in one God but does not accept Muhammad as a prophet.
wrong.1: Christianity centres on Jesus as the Son of God, not Muhammad.
wrong.3: Buddhism does not depend on a creator God or prophets.
